topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatment strategies and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Treatments and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic agents, highlighting their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cellular and Genetic Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that leverage specific cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the targeting of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the clinical challenges associated with off-target effects, bypass pathways, resistance, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail therapeutic strategies that use engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore tumor immune surveillance and methods for harnessing the immune system against cancer, including checkpoint inhibitors, neoantigen targeting, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Progress, Challenges, and Future Perspectives in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review historical gains in patient survival, current clinical challenges surrounding heterogeneity and resistance, and emerging directions and ethical considerations in oncology.
